LESSON: SINGING GAMES

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Singing games

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Singing games. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What songs do you sing able to:- games from the locality and from during play?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games
2. practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SINGING GAMES
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Singing games helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SINGING GAMES
Study Singing games like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games

What this means
In this part you learn to perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Singing games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share

What this means
In this part you learn to practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Singing games in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Singing games is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Singing games” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Singing games in your own words. (skill: practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Singing games to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games.
3. Practise this skill: practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Singing games from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Singing games: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Singing games?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What songs do you sing able to:- games from the locality and from during play?
2. when performing • Learners perform age-appropriate and other cultures for singing games?
3. Which games can we for enjoyment, coordinated body movements play as we sing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Singing games means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform singing games • Learners are guided to observe safety while observing own and others safety, while performing singing games.
5. Be able to: practice game etiquette • Individually and in groups, learners for integrity observe game etiquette and share.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
